walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Geography: Fluvial & Coastal Environments — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Geography: Fluvial & Coastal Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Geography: Fluvial & Coastal Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.

mcqs.q: Why are urbanisation rates currently higher in LICs than HICs?
options: Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
LICs have higher urbanisation rates because they have more cities than HICs.
HICs urbanised earlier and are now near saturation (80%+ urban); LICs are still in the rapid urbanisation phase, with high rural-urban migration and urban natural increase.
